title: Enforce per-task file restrictions from planner in implement phase
summary: Architecture analysis for adding per-task file restriction enforcement to the gateway. When the orchestrator spawns an implement agent, the gateway restricts that agent's commits to only the files listed in its assigned tasks' files_affected lists (with directory-sibling expansion and glob support). The recommended approach adds an allowed_files field to the Session model, uses warn-then-block enforcement at push time, and provides an egg-contract request-file escape hatch for observability. This builds on existing PhaseFileRestriction infrastructure with minimal new abstractions.

problem_statement.description: Phase-level file restrictions in the implement phase block .egg-state/ directories but allow modification of any code file. When multiple implement agents work in parallel (Tier 3 dispatch), agent A can accidentally modify files that belong to agent B's task, creating cross-contamination. The planner already produces per-task files_affected lists, but these are purely informational today. The goal is to make them an enforced boundary at the gateway level.
goals: Make the planner's per-task files list an enforced boundary, not just informational context
Warn on first out-of-scope file per session, block on repeated violations (guide, don't cage)
Support glob patterns in files_affected (e.g., src/components/*, tests/**)
Apply directory-sibling expansion: listing dir/foo.py implicitly allows other files in dir/
Filter post-agent auto-commits to exclude out-of-scope files (restore instead of commit)
Graceful fallback: empty files_affected = no per-file restriction
Provide egg-contract request-file escape hatch for observability when agents need out-of-scope files
Ensure Tier 3 parallel agent dispatch correctly scopes each agent to its task's file union

session_model.mechanism: Session dataclass carries phase, agent_role, pipeline_id, complexity_tier, and other metadata. Persisted to JSON on disk. No field exists for per-session file allowlists. register_session() at line 453-530 accepts all current fields but not allowed_files.
session_model.gap: No mechanism to pass task-scoped file restrictions from orchestrator to gateway.

phase_file_restrictions.mechanism: PhaseFileRestriction dataclass has allowed_patterns and blocked_patterns fields with glob matching via fnmatch. The implement phase uses only blocked_patterns (lines 510-519): blocks .egg-state/contracts/*, drafts/*, pipelines/*, reviews/* but has NO allowed_patterns, so all code files pass.
phase_file_restrictions.key_method: is_file_allowed() at line 183 checks blocked patterns first, then allowed patterns. _matches_pattern() at line 231 supports wildcard (fnmatch), directory prefix (endswith /), and prefix matching.
phase_file_restrictions.integration: check_phase_file_restrictions() called at gateway.py:789 during push validation and post_agent_commit.py:192 during auto-commit filtering.

push_validation_flow.mechanism: Push handler at line 486 uses @require_session_auth. Session stored in g.session. Three layers of file checks: (1) implementer role check (line 679), (2) agent-role restrictions (line 711, warn-only by default), (3) phase-based file restrictions (line 789). Changed files retrieved via get_changed_files_in_push(). All checks run on the same changed_files list.
push_validation_flow.insertion_point: Per-session file restrictions should be checked after phase restrictions (line 822) since they are a refinement of the phase-level allow-all-code policy.

post_agent_commit.mechanism: auto_commit_worktree() filters uncommitted changes by phase restrictions (lines 183-206). Blocked files are restored via git checkout (line 208-217). Allowed files selectively staged (line 231). Push goes through gateway for re-validation (lines 286-315).
post_agent_commit.gap: Only applies phase-level restrictions. No access to session's allowed_files at auto-commit time. Needs either the session token to look up allowed_files, or the allowed_files list passed directly.

agent_role_restrictions.mechanism: Separate system from phase restrictions. AgentFilePattern defines per-role allowed/blocked patterns. INTEGRATOR_TIER3_PATTERNS (line 325) gives Tier 3 integrators expanded write access. Checked at gateway.py:711, warn-only by default (EGG_AGENT_RESTRICTIONS_ENFORCE).
agent_role_restrictions.relationship: Agent-role restrictions and per-task restrictions are orthogonal. Role restrictions define what a coder can write (e.g., src/, not docs/). Task restrictions further narrow that to specific files within the role's scope.

container_spawner.mechanism: spawn_agent_container() calls self.gateway.register_session() with container_id, container_ip, mode, phase, pipeline_id, agent_role, issue_number, branch, complexity_tier. Does NOT read files_affected from the contract or pass them to the session.
container_spawner.gap: The spawner has access to the contract (and thus task files_affected) but doesn't extract or forward this data.

gateway_client.mechanism: register_session() makes POST to /api/v1/sessions/create. Parameters include phase, pipeline_id, agent_role, complexity_tier. No allowed_files parameter exists.
gateway_client.gap: Client API needs a new allowed_files parameter.

task_files_affected.mechanism: Task model has files_affected: list[str] (default empty). Plan parser extracts from YAML code fence (task_data.get('files', [])). Also supports markdown bracket extraction ([file1, file2]) and string-to-list normalization.
task_files_affected.status: Data is available in the contract. Just needs to be read by the container spawner and forwarded to session registration.

gateway_session_create_endpoint.mechanism: POST /api/v1/sessions/create accepts container_id, container_ip, mode, and optional phase, pipeline_id, agent_role, complexity_tier, branch. Calls session_manager.register_session(). Returns session_token.
gateway_session_create_endpoint.gap: Needs to accept and validate allowed_files parameter.

egg_contract_cli.mechanism: Supports show, add-commit, update-notes, add-decision, add-feedback subcommands. No request-file subcommand exists.
egg_contract_cli.gap: The escape hatch CLI (egg-contract request-file) needs to be built.

approaches.name: Session-scoped allowed_files with warn-then-block (issue's design)
approaches.description: Add allowed_files: list[str] | None to Session. Container spawner reads task files_affected, applies directory-sibling expansion, passes to register_session(). Gateway checks session allowed_files at push time after phase restrictions. First violation per file logs warning and allows push. Second violation for same file blocks push with actionable error. Post-agent commit filtering also applies session restrictions. egg-contract request-file escape hatch auto-approves and adds file to session's allowed_files.
pros: Directly implements the issue's specification and design philosophy
Reuses existing PhaseFileRestriction pattern matching infrastructure
Warn-then-block is forgiving for agents acting in good faith
Directory-sibling expansion handles helper/test file creation naturally
Escape hatch provides observability without blocking legitimate needs
Violation tracking is simple (dict[str, int] on Session)
Graceful fallback when allowed_files is None (backward compat)
cons: Violation tracking state must persist across pushes within a session
Directory-sibling expansion rules need careful scoping to avoid over-permissiveness
Two-strike model has edge cases: what if an agent intentionally touches a file, gets warned, then does it again in a legitimate follow-up push?
Escape hatch API adds a new gateway endpoint

approaches.name: Immediate soft-block with auto-approve escape hatch
approaches.description: Same session model changes, but every out-of-scope file immediately triggers a soft block with an actionable error directing the agent to use egg-contract request-file. The request auto-approves (with logging) and the agent retries the push.
pros: Simpler implementation — no violation counter state
Every out-of-scope access is explicitly logged via escape hatch
Consistent behavior from the first push — no ambiguity about when blocking happens
Cleaner audit trail since every exception is explicitly requested
cons: More friction: every out-of-scope file requires explicit request-file + retry cycle
Agents with incomplete planner file lists will spin on request-file calls
Contradicts the issue's 'guide, don't cage' and 'warn before block' principles
Latency cost: each out-of-scope file adds a round-trip to request-file + retry push

approaches.name: Warn-only with post-agent-commit filtering (no push-time blocking)
approaches.description: Add allowed_files to sessions and check at push time, but only ever log warnings — never block pushes. Rely on post-agent-commit filtering to prevent out-of-scope files from being permanently committed. No escape hatch needed since nothing is blocked.
pros: Zero risk of agents spinning due to incorrect file lists
Full observability into cross-contamination via structured warnings
Can be promoted to blocking later once planner quality is proven
Simplest implementation — no violation tracking, no escape hatch API
cons: Post-agent-commit filtering silently drops files, confusing when agent thinks it committed successfully
Doesn't prevent cross-contamination at push time — only catches it at auto-commit
If agent pushes successfully, other agents pulling the branch see out-of-scope changes
Doesn't meet the issue's acceptance criteria which require blocking on repeated violations

recommended_approach.name: Session-scoped allowed_files with warn-then-block
justification: This approach directly implements the issue's specification, which was detailed and specific about the warn-then-block model, directory-sibling expansion, and escape hatch design. The refine analysis (805-analysis.md) also recommended Option A, and both refine reviewers approved it.

The existing PhaseFileRestriction infrastructure (phase_filter.py) already has the pattern matching code needed: _matches_pattern() supports fnmatch globs, directory prefixes, and prefix matching. The new per-session check reuses this code rather than building a parallel system.

Warn-then-block is the right tradeoff for this use case. The enforcement catches accidental cross-contamination (the common case in Tier 3 parallel dispatch) while avoiding blocking agents with legitimate needs. The escape hatch (egg-contract request-file) handles the exception case with full observability.

The Session model already carries per-session metadata (phase, agent_role, pipeline_id, complexity_tier). Adding allowed_files and file_warnings follows the established pattern. Both serialize naturally to JSON for persistence.

technical_decisions.decision: Store allowed_files on the Session dataclass rather than a separate store
technical_decisions.rationale: The Session already carries per-session metadata (phase, agent_role, pipeline_id, complexity_tier). Adding allowed_files follows the same pattern. Sessions are persisted to JSON — the list serializes naturally. No new storage mechanism needed.
alternatives_considered: Separate FileRestrictionStore keyed by session hash — rejected: fragments session state across two persistence systems
Extend PhaseFileRestriction with per-session overlays — rejected: PhaseFileRestriction is phase-scoped, not session-scoped. Per-session data on a phase-scoped structure conflates two concepts.

technical_decisions.decision: Apply directory-sibling expansion at the container spawner (client-side), not the gateway (server-side)
technical_decisions.rationale: The container spawner is where task assignment happens and has full context about the plan structure. Expanding at the spawner means the gateway receives an already-expanded list and doesn't need to know about the expansion rules. This keeps the gateway's file matching logic simple and reusable. The gateway just does pattern matching on whatever list it receives.
alternatives_considered: Expand at gateway during session creation — rejected: gateway shouldn't need plan-structure awareness. Keeping gateway stateless about plan semantics preserves separation of concerns.
Expand at check time (lazy) — rejected: repeating expansion on every push wastes cycles and makes debugging harder since the effective list isn't visible in the session

technical_decisions.decision: Violation tracking as dict[str, int] on Session, not persisted across gateway restarts
technical_decisions.rationale: The file_warnings dict maps normalized file paths to violation counts. It persists across pushes within a session (which is the normal case — agents push multiple times). Resetting on gateway restart is acceptable because: (1) gateway restarts during an agent session are rare, (2) the worst case is the agent gets one extra warning before being blocked, (3) simpler than introducing a separate violation store.
alternatives_considered: Persist violations to session JSON — considered acceptable and low-effort, but adds persistence overhead for a rare edge case. Decision: persist to session JSON for robustness since we're already serializing the session.
In-memory only with TTL — rejected: doesn't survive the session save/load cycle that happens on every session update

technical_decisions.decision: Per-session check runs AFTER phase-level and role-level checks, not instead of
technical_decisions.rationale: The three restriction layers (phase, role, per-session task scope) are independent and cumulative. Phase restrictions are the primary security boundary. Role restrictions scope by agent type. Per-session task restrictions narrow further to the specific files assigned. A file must pass all three checks. Per-session check runs last because it's the most granular and has the warn-then-block behavior that should only trigger after the hard security checks have passed.
alternatives_considered: Replace phase restrictions with per-session restrictions for implement phase — rejected: phase restrictions are the authoritative security gate. Per-session is defense-in-depth, not a replacement.
Merge per-session into phase restrictions dynamically — rejected: conflates static security policy with dynamic per-session scope. Harder to audit and debug.

technical_decisions.decision: Escape hatch auto-approves in initial implementation, strict mode deferred
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue mentions egg-contract request-file could 'auto-approve or queue a HITL decision for strict mode.' Auto-approve serves the primary use case: observability. Every exception is logged with the agent's reason, creating an audit trail without blocking the agent. Strict mode (HITL approval required) can be added later behind a config flag when there's evidence it's needed. Over-engineering the escape hatch risks making it unused.
alternatives_considered: Strict mode from day one — rejected: adds HITL queue integration complexity for a feature that may not be needed. The issue calls this out as a future option.
No escape hatch (rely on planner quality) — rejected: issue explicitly requires it for observability

technical_decisions.decision: Directory-sibling expansion scoped to immediate parent directory, not ancestors
technical_decisions.rationale: Listing src/auth/login.py allows other files in src/auth/ but NOT all of src/. This is generous enough for the common case (creating helper files and tests next to implementation files) without being so permissive that listing any file in src/ gives access to the entire directory tree. The expansion adds the parent directory as a prefix pattern (src/auth/).
alternatives_considered: Multi-level expansion (allow all ancestor directories) — rejected: listing one file in src/ would allow writing anything in src/, defeating the purpose
No directory expansion (exact files only) — rejected: too strict. Agents commonly create helper files and tests next to their implementation files. The issue explicitly requires this.
Configurable expansion depth — rejected: over-engineering. Parent directory is the right granularity.

technical_decisions.decision: No hardcoded config file allowlist — planner responsibility with template guidance
technical_decisions.rationale: The refine analysis raised whether common config files (pyproject.toml, package.json, Makefile) should be implicitly allowed. The answer is no: a hardcoded allowlist in the gateway couples it to language/framework conventions and creates a maintenance burden. Instead, the plan template should guide the planner to include config files that the task will touch. The directory-sibling expansion already helps: if the planner lists any file in the repo root, other root files are accessible.
alternatives_considered: Hardcoded allowlist of common config files — rejected: couples gateway to language conventions, hard to maintain, may be overly permissive
Project-level config allowlist in .egg/phase-permissions.json — considered for future iteration. Would let repo owners declare always-allowed config files. Not needed in v1.

technical_decisions.decision: Violation tracking persisted in session JSON alongside allowed_files
technical_decisions.rationale: After further consideration (per TD-3), persisting file_warnings to the session JSON is the right call. Sessions are already saved to disk atomically after every update. Adding a dict[str, int] field is trivial. This ensures violations survive across session reloads and provides a complete audit trail in the persisted session state. The overhead is negligible since sessions are small JSON objects.
alternatives_considered: In-memory only — rejected per TD-3 analysis: doesn't survive session save/load cycles

risks.description: Planner produces incomplete files_affected lists, causing agents to spin on warnings/blocks
risks.mitigation: Three-layer defense: (1) directory-sibling expansion makes exact listing unnecessary, (2) warn-then-block gives agents a chance to self-correct before being blocked, (3) egg-contract request-file escape hatch auto-approves with logging. Additionally, empty files_affected = no restriction (graceful fallback). Plan template updated with guidance on generous listing.

risks.description: Session allowed_files list grows unbounded via request-file escape hatch
risks.mitigation: Cap allowed_files at 500 entries (validated at session creation and request-file). If an agent needs more than 500 file patterns, the planner's file list is fundamentally broken and needs human intervention. Log a warning at 100 entries.

risks.description: Push validation latency increases due to per-session file matching
risks.mitigation: The existing _matches_pattern() uses fnmatch which is efficient for small pattern lists (<500). File matching runs after the changed_files list is already computed. For typical sessions with 5-50 file patterns and 1-20 changed files, matching is O(N*M) = O(1000) comparisons, which is negligible.

risks.description: Directory-sibling expansion is too permissive for top-level directories
risks.mitigation: Expansion only adds parent directory prefix. Listing a file at the repo root (e.g., setup.py) would add '/' prefix allowing all root files — but not subdirectories. For subdirectories, listing src/module/foo.py adds src/module/ prefix, which is appropriately scoped. Edge case: listing src/foo.py adds src/ prefix which is broad. Mitigation: planner guidance to use specific subdirectories, and the directory expansion should handle repo-root files specially (only allow other root-level files, not subdirectory trees).

risks.description: Race condition between push and request-file API calls
risks.mitigation: The session's allowed_files list is modified by request-file and read by push validation. Both run in the Flask request handler. The SessionManager uses thread locking for session modifications. No race condition because Flask handles requests sequentially per session (agents push sequentially).

risks.description: Post-agent auto-commit cannot access session allowed_files if session expired
risks.mitigation: The auto-commit trigger should capture allowed_files at container exit time, before session cleanup. Alternatively, the allowed_files can be passed as a parameter to auto_commit_worktree() rather than looking them up from the session. If neither is available, fall back to phase-only filtering (current behavior).

risks.description: Backward compatibility: existing sessions without allowed_files field
risks.mitigation: allowed_files defaults to None on the Session dataclass. from_persistence() uses .get('allowed_files', None) for backward compatibility. When None, per-session file checks are skipped entirely (current behavior preserved).

constraints: Sessions without allowed_files (non-pipeline, non-implement, or pre-existing) must behave identically to today
Empty files_affected on tasks = no per-file restriction (graceful fallback)
Phase-level restrictions remain the primary security boundary — per-session restrictions are defense-in-depth
Agent-role restrictions remain independent and are checked separately
Per-session file matching must reuse existing _matches_pattern() infrastructure for consistency
Violation tracking must persist within a session (survive session save/load cycles)
Gateway HTTP API changes must be backward-compatible (allowed_files is optional)
Post-agent auto-commit filtering must log clearly, not silently drop files
Escape hatch must auto-approve in v1 (strict mode deferred)

Q1_config_file_allowlisting.question: Should the gateway maintain a hardcoded allowlist of common config files that bypass per-task restrictions?
Q1_config_file_allowlisting.resolution: No hardcoded allowlist. Planner responsibility with template guidance. Directory-sibling expansion handles the common case. See TD-7.

Q2_strict_mode_escape_hatch.question: Is strict mode (HITL approval required) needed for egg-contract request-file in the initial implementation?
Q2_strict_mode_escape_hatch.resolution: Auto-approve only in v1. Strict mode deferred. See TD-5.

Q3_restriction_ordering.question: Should per-task restrictions be evaluated before or after role restrictions?
Q3_restriction_ordering.resolution: After both phase and role restrictions. Per-session is the most granular layer and runs last. Role restrictions still win if they block a file. See TD-4.

Q4_directory_expansion_scope.question: How broadly should directory-sibling expansion apply?
Q4_directory_expansion_scope.resolution: Immediate parent directory only. Listing src/auth/login.py allows src/auth/* but not src/*. See TD-6.
